decisions.reason: As a simple extension of the bakery’s core bread range, it is cheap to carry and there is no clear negative signal yet, so the option value of waiting still exceeds the likely cost.
The repeat gold medal is strong evidence of product quality and marketability, so management would very likely continue backing this successful seasonal line.
This seeded rye-mix bread fits existing capabilities and ingredients closely, and with no bad evidence its low-cost experimentation value supports keeping it for now.

Although this is a somewhat more niche rye variant and the firm already has several similar bread options, its carrying cost is still low enough that management would likely keep it until demand becomes clearer.

The marzipan stollen is a seasonal variant close to the established confectionery offer, so despite lacking a visible success signal its downside is limited and it remains worth keeping another season.
As the newest differentiated bread using ancient grains, it offers unresolved upside with little extra capability investment, which makes preserving the option attractive.
